key_insight: Decoupling pose from shape yields a pose-aware retrieval pipeline that is more interpretable and robust to occlusions in single-view 3D shape retrieval.
problem_solved: Improves single-view 3D shape retrieval under heavy occlusion and arbitrary camera poses, addressing the limited interpretability and poor generalization of holistic feed-forward alignment methods.
method: Pose-aware representation: disentangle or estimate view pose to normalize observations before shape matching.
Occlusion-aware feature extraction: focus on visible parts (e.g., visibility masks or attention) to produce robust partial-shape descriptors.
Pose-normalized retrieval: match query embeddings to 3D shape embeddings in a common, interpretable space (e.g., with contrastive or alignment supervision) to improve robustness and explainability.
impact: Makes 3D retrieval systems more reliable in real-world scenarios (e.g., robotics, AR, and large-scale image-to-3D search) by handling occlusion and pose variation while providing interpretable retrieval cues for debugging and downstream use.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: input image → pose estimator / visibility mask → pose-normalization → shape embedding → retrieval results
Before/after retrieval examples: occluded query images with top-k retrieved 3D shapes for baseline vs. PASR
Embedding visualization: 2D projection (t-SNE/UMAP) showing better clustering after pose normalization
Attention/visibility overlay: heatmaps or masks on input images illustrating which visible parts drive retrieval
paper_title: PASR: Pose-Aware 3D Shape Retrieval from Occluded Single Views
paper_authors: Jiaxin Shi, Guofeng Zhang, Wufei Ma, Naifu Liang, Adam Kortylewski
